mainTopic: Open and closed letters (סתום and פתוח), the miraculous לוחות, and the children's דרשות on the letters of the אלף-בית
overview: This amud begins by explaining why turning an open letter into a closed one is fine, but turning a closed letter into an open one is a problem. The reason given is that closed letters like ם and ס stood by a miracle on the לוחות, while the double forms of מנצפ"ך were said to come from the צופים (prophets). The גמרא objects that a נביא may not add anything new, based on 'אלה המצות'. It concludes that both forms come from סיני, were forgotten, and were later restored. Next the גמרא returns to רב חסדא's teachings about the miraculous writing on the לוחות. Then comes an אגדה about young children who explained the letters of the אלף-בית as lessons about Torah study, צדקה, humility, תשובה, and truth versus falsehood. The amud ends with letter codes (אתב"ש, then אח"ס בט"ע, then אלב"ם) that describe the fate of the רשעים and the צדיקים. In the closing dialogue, God refuses to hand the צדיקים over to גיהנם.

steps.title: Closing an open letter raises its status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why turning an open letter into a closed one is acceptable: closed letters have special status, because ם and ס stood by a miracle on the לוחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is raising its status. As רב חסדא said: the ם and the ס that were on the לוחות stood in place by a miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining the previous ruling: if an open letter was made closed, it is fine, because closing a letter 'upgrades' it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters on the לוחות were carved all the way through the stone. In a fully closed letter like ם or ס, the middle piece should have fallen out, but it miraculously stayed. That miracle shows closed letters have a special, higher status.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tablets of the Ten Commandments

steps.confusionAlert: The ם here is the final, closed mem. It is not the open מ used in the middle of a word.

phrases.english: he is elevating it,
phrases.notes: This is about an open letter that got written closed.

phrases.english: as Rav Ḥisda said:
the mem and samekh that were on the Tablets
phrases.notes: He means the closed mem, the one used at the end of a word.

phrases.english: were standing by a miracle.
phrases.notes: Their inner pieces did not fall out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier's discussion of open/closed letters by giving the reason for the lenient case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Open-made-closed is valid because closed letters have higher status, proven by the miracle of ם and ס on the לוחות.

steps.title: Opening a closed letter lowers its status
steps.stepSummary: Turning a closed letter into an open one is explained as 'downgrading' it, because the open/closed forms of מנצפ"ך were supposedly introduced later by the צופים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he took a closed letter and made it open, he lowers its status. As רבי ירמיה said, and some say it was רבי חייא בר אבא: the letters מנצפ"ך were instituted by the צופים (prophets).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the stricter case: making a closed letter open is a downgrade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The closed letters go back to the לוחות at סיני. If the prophets added the extra forms later, those newer forms are less important. Changing a closed letter into one of them lowers its status.

keyTerms.meaning: The five letters that have a separate final form: מ, נ, צ, פ, כ

phrases.english: But a closed letter that he made open —
he is diminishing it,
as Rabbi Yirmeya said,
and some say it was Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba:
Mem-nun-tzadi-peh-kaf — the prophets instituted them.
phrases.notes: He means the second form each of these letters has.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation by giving the reason for the strict case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Closed-made-open is invalid because it downgrades the letter into a later, prophet-instituted form.

steps.title: Prophets cannot add anything new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the prophets introduced the forms of מנצפ"ך, since a prophet may not add anything new to the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think so?! Isn't it written: 'These are the commandments'? From that we learn that a prophet is not allowed to introduce anything new from now on!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason given in step 2 that the צופים created the forms of מנצפ"ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלה' ('these') teaches that only these מצוות, given at סיני, are the Torah. No later נביא can add new Torah elements. So prophets could not have invented new letter forms.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so?! (an opening for a challenge)

phrases.english: And can you understand that?!
But isn't it written: 'These are the commandments' —
that a prophet is not permitted
to introduce anything new from now on!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the premise of step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק teaches that no prophet may add new Torah elements, so prophets could not have instituted new letter forms.

steps.title: The forms existed; the prophets fixed their positions
steps.stepSummary: Answer: both forms already existed, but people did not know which goes in the middle of a word and which at the end. The צופים set the positions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the forms did exist, but people did not know which one goes in the middle of a word and which goes at the end of a word. Then the prophets came and set them in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets 'צופים אמרום' to mean the prophets only assigned the placement of the forms. They did not invent them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tries to avoid adding a new thing: the shapes came from סיני. The prophets only organized where each shape is used.

phrases.english: Rather, they did exist,
but they did not know

phrases.aramaic: הֵי בְּאֶמְצַע תֵּיבָה הֵי בְּסוֹף תֵּיבָה,
phrases.english: which goes in the middle of a word and which at the end of a word,
and the prophets came and established them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prophets invented the double letter forms.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forms existed from סיני; the prophets only fixed which goes in the middle and which goes at the end.

steps.title: Even setting positions is something new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses again: even fixing the positions would be a new addition, which a נביא may not make.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, 'These are the commandments' teaches that a prophet may not introduce anything new from now on!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the answer in step 4 does not fully work, and repeats the same פסוק as a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Deciding which form goes where is still a new rule about how the Torah is written. That would still count as a prophet adding something.

phrases.english: And still: 'These are the commandments' —
that a prophet is not permitted
to introduce anything new from now on!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the challenge of step 3 against the answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the prophets set the positions of the letter forms
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fixing positions is also an innovation, which 'אלה המצות' forbids.

steps.title: Forgotten and then restored
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: the positions were given at סיני, were forgotten over time, and the prophets restored them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they forgot them, and the prophets went back and re-established them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the prophets did not add anything. They brought back what had been forgotten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Restoring forgotten Torah is not 'adding', so 'אלה המצות' is not broken. This means both forms come from סיני. So the earlier idea that open forms are 'newer' and lower in status is no longer supported.
steps.whatToRemember: Both the open and closed forms of מנצפ"ך go back to סיני. The prophets only restored their positions after they were forgotten, because a נביא cannot add anything new to the Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule: later authorities can restore forgotten Torah, but they cannot create new Torah law as prophets.

phrases.english: Rather, they forgot them
and they went back and re-established them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the renewed challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prophets set the letter positions for the first time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The positions came from סיני, were forgotten, and were restored by the prophets.

steps.title: Returning to רב חסדא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: Using 'גופא', the גמרא goes back to examine רב חסדא's statement about the miraculous ם and ס on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: רב חסדא said: the ם and ס on the לוחות stood by a miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב חסדא's statement to set up a discussion of his teachings about the לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, this statement was quoted only as a proof. Now the גמרא repeats it on purpose so it can add another teaching from רב חסדא about the לוחות.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: returning to analyze a statement that was quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Ḥisda said:
the mem and samekh that were on the Tablets
were standing by a miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a statement quoted in step 1, now as its own topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The closed ם and ס on the לוחות stood miraculously.

steps.title: The Tablets could be read from both sides
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds that the writing on the לוחות could be read from both sides, with the letters appearing reversed from the back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא also said: the writing on the לוחות could be read from the inside and from the outside. For example: נבוב reads as בובן, רהב as בהר, סרו as ורס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second miracle teaching about the לוחות from רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the letters were carved all the way through, someone looking from the back saw the words in reverse order. The examples show what a word looks like when read backward.
steps.confusionAlert: These example words (נבוב, רהב, סרו) come from other places in תנ"ך. They were not written on the לוחות. They only show what reversed reading looks like.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:
the writing on the Tablets was read from the inside
and read from the outside,
for example: 'navuv' read as 'b-v-b-n',
'rahav' read as 'bahar',
'saru' read as 'v-r-s'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related teaching by the same אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The writing on the לוחות was readable from both sides, appearing reversed on one side.

steps.title: Young students say amazing new things
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רבי יהושע בן לוי that young children came to the בית מדרש and said insights never heard even in the days of יהושע בן נון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבי יהושע בן לוי: young children came to the בית מדרש today and said things that were not said even in the days of יהושע בן נון.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. It opens a story and prepares us for the children's teachings about the אלף-בית, which come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from letters on the לוחות to the meaning of the letters themselves. The story highlights how impressive these insights are, since they come from young children.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
young children came today to the study hall
and said things
that even in the days of Joshua bin Nun
nothing like them was said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new אגדה about the letters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the children's דרשות on the אלף-בית.

steps.title: אלף-בית means learn wisdom; גימל-דלת means help the poor
steps.stepSummary: The children read the letter names as lessons: אלף בית means 'learn wisdom', and גימל דלת means 'give to the poor'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alef-beis means 'אלף בינה', learn wisdom. Gimmel-dalet means 'גמול דלים', give kindness to the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The children explain the letter names as messages: first Torah study, then צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair of letter names is read as a phrase that sounds similar. אלף becomes 'learn' and בית becomes 'בינה'. גימל becomes 'bestow' and דלת becomes 'דלים'.

phrases.english: Alef beit — learn wisdom.
Gimmel dalet — give to the poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the children's teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The letter names carry messages of Torah learning and kindness to the poor.

steps.title: The ג's leg reaches toward the ד
steps.stepSummary: The gimmel's foot stretches toward the dalet because a person who does חסד should run after the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is the leg of the gimmel stretched toward the dalet? Because the way of one who does kindness is to run after the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The children explain the shape of the gimmel: its leg 'runs' toward the dalet, which stands for the poor person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The giver (gimmel) should not wait for the poor to come. He should actively go looking for them.

keyTerms.meaning: One who does acts of kindness

phrases.english: Why is the leg of the gimmel extended
toward the dalet —
because it is the way of one who bestows kindness
to run after the poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on 'גמול דלים' using the shape of the letter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A giver should actively seek out the poor.

steps.title: The ד's leg reaches toward the ג
steps.stepSummary: The dalet's leg stretches toward the gimmel because the poor person should make himself available to the giver.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is the leg of the dalet stretched toward the gimmel? So that the poor person makes himself available to the giver.
steps.whatsHappening: The children explain the dalet's shape: the poor person also moves toward the giver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Helping the poor works from both sides. The giver runs after the poor, and the poor person makes himself easy to find.

keyTerms.meaning: That he make himself available to him

phrases.english: And why is the leg of the dalet extended
toward the gimmel —
so that he makes himself available to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching lesson from the dalet's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The poor person should make himself reachable to those who want to give.

steps.title: The ד faces away: give privately
steps.stepSummary: The dalet faces away from the gimmel to teach that צדקה should be given privately, so the poor person is not embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does the dalet turn its face away from the gimmel? So that the giver gives to him privately, so that the poor person will not be embarrassed in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The children explain one more detail of the dalet: it faces away, which teaches that צדקה should be given quietly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the two letters reach toward each other, the poor person's 'face' is turned away. This shows that צדקה should be given without face-to-face shame, protecting the dignity of the person receiving it.
steps.whatToRemember: The shapes of ג and ד teach how to give צדקה: the giver runs after the poor, the poor person makes himself available, and the giving should be private to protect his dignity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the value of מתן בסתר, giving צדקה in a way that does not embarrass the person receiving it.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי טַעְמָא מְהַדַּר אַפֵּיהּ דְּדָלֶ״ת מִגִּימֶ״ל —
phrases.english: And why does the dalet turn its face away from the gimmel —
so that he gives to him discreetly,
so that he will not be embarrassed by him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא מְהַדַּר אַפֵּיהּ דְּדָלֶ״ת מִגִּימֶ״ל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the lessons drawn from the shapes of ג and ד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדקה should be given privately to spare the poor person embarrassment.

steps.title: ה״ו: The Name of God
steps.stepSummary: The letters ה and ו are read as part of the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Heh-Vav: this is the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
steps.whatsHappening: The children move to the next pair of letters, ה and ו. They say these letters stand for the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה and ו are letters in the four-letter name of God (י-ה-ו-ה). After teaching that one should give to the poor, the children now point to God, the One who sees and rewards that giving.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of the Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.aramaic: ה״ו — זֶה שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
phrases.english: Heh-Vav: this is the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
phrases.notes: Heh and vav are letters of the Divine Name.

steps.triggerLanguage: ה״ו — זֶה שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the children's letter-by-letter lessons after גימל-דלת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה״ו stands for the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא.

steps.title: ז through ל: The Reward for Giving
steps.stepSummary: The letters ז״ח ט״י כ״ל spell out the rewards God gives to one who acts this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Zayin-Chet, Tet-Yud, Kaf-Lamed: if you do this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, feeds you, shows you favor, does good for you, gives you an inheritance, and ties a crown for you in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The children read the next six letters as first letters of rewards. If you give צדקה the right way, God gives you all these good things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter begins a reward word: ז for זן (feeds), ח for חן (favor), ט for מטיב (does good), י for ירושה (inheritance), כ for כתר (crown), and ל for לעולם הבא. This finishes the lesson begun with גימל-דלת.
steps.confusionAlert: Not every reward word starts with its letter in an obvious way. מֵטִיב is matched to ט because of its root טוב, and לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא is matched to ל.

phrases.english: Zayin-Chet, Tet-Yud, Kaf-Lamed:
and if you do so,
phrases.notes: That is, giving to the poor, and doing it privately.

phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, feeds you,
phrases.notes: The ז stands for זן, 'feeds.'

phrases.english: and shows you favor, and does good for you,
phrases.notes: ח stands for חן, and ט for מטיב, from the word טוב.

phrases.english: and gives you an inheritance,
phrases.notes: י stands for ירושה, 'inheritance.'

phrases.english: and ties a crown for you in the World to Come.
phrases.notes: כ stands for כתר, 'crown,' and ל for לעולם הבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: ז״ח ט״י כ״ל — וְאִם אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reward for the צדקה described in the גימל-דלת lessons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who gives צדקה properly receives food, favor, goodness, inheritance, and a crown in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Open and Closed מ: Open and Hidden Teachings
steps.stepSummary: The open מ and closed ם teach that the Torah has open teachings and hidden teachings.
steps.simpleTranslation: An open mem and a closed mem stand for an open statement and a closed statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The children explain why מ has two forms, open (מ) and closed at the end of a word (ם). They say the Torah has teachings everyone can understand and teachings that are hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The open shape matches an 'open' teaching that is plain to everyone. The closed shape matches a 'closed' teaching, meaning deeper secrets of Torah.

phrases.english: Open mem, closed mem:
an open statement, a closed statement.
phrases.notes: He means Torah teachings that are plain, and ones that are hidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from letter names to letter shapes, starting with the double forms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah contains both revealed and hidden teachings.

steps.title: Bent and Straight נ: The Humble Faithful Person
steps.stepSummary: The bent נ and the straight ן teach that a humble faithful person will end up standing tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bent nun and a straight nun stand for a faithful person who is bent and a faithful person who is straight.
steps.whatsHappening: The children explain the two forms of נ: bent (נ) and straight at the end of a word (ן). A faithful person who is humble and bent now will later stand tall and be known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נ stands for נאמן (faithful). The bent shape comes first and the straight one comes at the end of the word. In the same way, humility now leads to standing tall later.

phrases.english: Bent nun, straight nun:
a faithful person who is bent, a faithful person who is straight.
phrases.notes: Humble now, and later upright and recognized.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next double letter after מ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A humble faithful person will in the end be raised up.

steps.title: ס״ע: Support the Poor, or Make Memory Signs
steps.stepSummary: ס״ע is read two ways: support the poor, or make memory signs for Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Samech-Ayin: support the poor. Another version: make memory signs in Torah and acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: The children read ס and ע as 'סמוך עניים', meaning support the poor. The גמרא then brings a second version that reads them as 'סימנין עשה', meaning make memory signs for your learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both readings use ס and ע as first letters. The first reading continues the צדקה theme. The second reading teaches a way of learning: use signs and memory aids so the Torah stays with you.

phrases.english: Samech-Ayin: support the poor.
phrases.notes: Hold them up so they do not fall further.

phrases.english: Another version:
make memory signs in the Torah and acquire it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to reading letter names after the shape-based נו״ן lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ס״ע means support the poor; or, by another version, make memory signs to keep your Torah.

steps.title: Bent and Straight פ: When to Speak and When to Be Silent
steps.stepSummary: The two forms of פ teach that sometimes the mouth should be open and sometimes closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bent peh and a straight peh stand for an open mouth and a closed mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The children explain the two forms of פ. There are times to speak and times to stay quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פ sounds like פה, meaning mouth. The two shapes show two right ways to use the mouth, speaking or holding back, each in its proper time.

phrases.english: Bent peh, straight peh:
an open mouth, a closed mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next double letter in the alphabet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a time to speak and a time to be silent.

steps.title: Bent and Straight צ: The Humble צדיק
steps.stepSummary: The two forms of צ teach that a humble צדיק will later stand tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bent tzadi and a straight tzadi stand for a righteous person who is bent and a righteous person who is straight.
steps.whatsHappening: The children explain the two forms of צ. A צדיק who is humble now will later be upright and known to all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern as the נו״ן lesson, now applied to a צדיק. That sameness sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.

phrases.english: Bent tzadi and straight tzadi:
a righteous person who is bent, a righteous person who is straight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next double letter; uses the same pattern as נו״ן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A humble צדיק will in the end be raised up.

steps.title: Isn't This the Same as the נ Lesson?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the צדי lesson repeats the נו״ן lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the same as 'a faithful person who is bent, a faithful person who is straight'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the צדי lesson. It seems to say exactly what the נו״ן lesson already said, so why repeat it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter is supposed to teach something new. If צדי only repeats נו״ן's idea of humble now and upright later, it seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: That is the same as: a faithful person bent, a faithful person straight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 20 as repeating step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It repeats the נו״ן lesson word for word in idea, so it seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: Double Bending: Torah Was Given With Awe
steps.stepSummary: The repetition adds extra bending, which teaches that Torah was given with deep humility and awe.
steps.simpleTranslation: The text added bending on top of his bending. From here we learn that the Torah was given with a bowed head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the repeat is on purpose. The extra 'bending' teaches that the Torah must be received with great humility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeat is not a waste. Bending twice, once for the נאמן and again for the צדיק, shows extra humility. That teaches that Torah was given 'במנוד ראש', with a bowed head and in an atmosphere of awe.

keyTerms.meaning: Shaking or bowing of the head; awe and seriousness

steps.whatToRemember: The two humility lessons (נו״ן and צדי) are not a repeat. Together they teach that Torah is received only with double humility and awe.

phrases.english: The text added for you
bending on top of his bending,
from here we learn that the Torah was given with a bowed head.
phrases.notes: With seriousness, awe, and humility.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹסִיף לְךָ הַכָּתוּב כְּפִיפָה עַל כְּפִיפָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the repetition as adding emphasis
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The צדי lesson is just a copy of the נו״ן lesson.
steps.terutzMaskana: The repetition doubles the humility, teaching that Torah was given with awe.

steps.title: ק and ר: God Turns Away From the Wicked
steps.stepSummary: ק stands for קדוש and ר for רשע; the ק faces away from the ר because God cannot look at the wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Kuf: holy. Reish: wicked. Why does the kuf turn its face away from the reish? The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: I cannot look at the wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The children read ק as קדוש (God) and ר as רשע (a wicked person). They explain that the letters face away from each other because God does not look at the wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the alphabet ר comes after ק, and their shapes point in different directions. The children read this as a picture of God and the רשע being turned away from each other.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrasing is a polite way of speaking (לשון נקיה). Really it is the רשע who turns away from God, but the גמרא speaks as if the ק turns away.

phrases.english: Kuf: holy.
Reish: wicked.
What is the reason it turns its face away,
the kuf from the reish?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I cannot look at the wicked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the children's letter lessons after the side discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God and the רשע are turned away from each other.

steps.title: The ק's Crown Points to the ר: Hope for the Penitent
steps.stepSummary: The crown of the ק points toward the ר, showing that if the רשע repents, God will crown him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is the crown of the kuf turned toward the reish? The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: If he repents, I will tie a crown for him like My own.
steps.whatsHappening: Even though the letters face apart, the little crown on top of the ק points toward the ר. This shows that God still wants the רשע to come back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This balances the last step. God turns away from evil, but He holds out a reward, a crown like His own, for the רשע who does תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Its crown (the small decorative stroke on a letter)

phrases.english: And what is the reason its crown is turned
(the kuf's) toward the reish?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
If he repents,
I tie for him a crown like My own.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא מְהַדַּר תָּגֵיהּ דְּקוּ״ף לְגַבֵּי רֵי״שׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a hopeful detail to the ק-ר picture.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רשע who does תשובה is crowned by God.

steps.title: The ק's Hanging Leg: A Door for תשובה
steps.stepSummary: The ק's leg hangs loose, leaving an opening so the penitent can come in.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does the kuf's leg hang? So that if he repents, he can enter.
steps.whatsHappening: The children point out that the leg of the ק does not touch its roof. That gap is an open door for the רשע to come back in through תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shape itself leaves room to return. This detail sets up the גמרא's next question about a different opening in the letter.

phrases.english: And what is the reason the kuf's leg hangs?
So that if he repents, he can enter.
phrases.notes: Through the gap between the leg and the roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third explanation of the ק's shape.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is always an opening for the בעל תשובה to return.

steps.title: Why Not Enter Through the Big Opening?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the penitent must use the small top gap when the ק is wide open at the bottom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him enter through that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last lesson. The ק is already open at the bottom, so why does the רשע need the small gap at the top?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bottom is wide open, the narrow top opening seems unnecessary. Why would a returning person take the hard way in?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him enter through that one

phrases.english: Let him enter through that one!
phrases.notes: Through the wide opening at the bottom of the kuf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the hanging leg is the door for the penitent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bottom of the ק is already open, so a special top opening seems pointless.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Heaven Helps Those Who Come to Purify
steps.stepSummary: The bottom opening is for one who goes out to sin; the top opening shows that the returning person gets special help, as ריש לקיש taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports ריש לקיש, as ריש לקיש said: What is meant by 'If it concerns the scorners, He scorns them, and to the humble He gives grace'? One who comes to become impure is given an opening; one who comes to become pure is helped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with ריש לקיש's teaching. The wide bottom opening is the way out for someone who wants to sin. The way back in is a special opening, because Heaven actively helps the one who returns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who wants to sin is only let go; he walks out the wide door. Someone who wants to become pure gets more than permission: Heaven helps him through a door made especially for him. So the ק's shape matches ריש לקיש's reading of the פסוק in משלי.
steps.whatToRemember: A person who wants to sin is only allowed to. A person who wants to do תשובה is actively helped by Heaven. The shape of the ק shows this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous teaching about תשובה: the first step back is met with help from שמים, not just permission.

phrases.english: This supports Reish Lakish,
as Reish Lakish said:
What is meant by that which is written:
'If it concerns the scorners, He scorns them,'
phrases.notes: משלי ג:לד

phrases.english: 'and to the humble He gives grace'?
One who comes to become impure is given an opening;
phrases.notes: He is not stopped, matching the wide bottom opening.

phrases.english: one who comes to become pure is helped.
phrases.notes: Matching the special top opening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26, using ריש לקיש's teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two openings by their function, supported by an outside אמורא's teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bottom opening could serve as the way back in, so the top gap is unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bottom is the way out for sinners; the special top opening shows Heaven's active help for the one who returns.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's reading of משלי ג:לד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shape of the ק supports ריש לקיש's teaching

steps.title: ש stands for falsehood, ת stands for truth
steps.stepSummary: The letter ש hints at שקר, and the letter ת hints at אמת.
steps.simpleTranslation: ש stands for falsehood (שקר). ת stands for truth (אמת).
steps.whatsHappening: The children continue their letter teachings and pair the last two letters with two opposite ideas: ש for שקר and ת for אמת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ש is the first letter of שקר, and ת is the last letter of אמת. This statement is the base for the two questions that follow, which compare how the two words look and where their letters sit in the alphabet.

keyTerms.meaning: The last two letters of the אלף-בית

phrases.english: Shin — falsehood.
Tav — truth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the letter-by-letter אגדה that explained ק and ר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ש represents שקר; ת represents אמת.

steps.title: Why are the letters of falsehood close together and the letters of truth far apart?
steps.stepSummary: The children ask why the letters of שקר sit side by side in the alphabet while the letters of אמת are spread out.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that the letters of 'שקר' are close to each other, while the letters of 'אמת' are far apart?
steps.whatsHappening: The children ask a question about letter order. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ק, ר, ש come one right after another near the end of the alphabet. א, מ, ת are spread out: the first letter, a middle letter, and the last letter. The question asks what lesson this spacing teaches.

phrases.english: What is the reason that falsehood's letters are close together,
while truth's letters are far apart?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the two words introduced in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind the spacing of the letters of שקר and אמת.

steps.title: Falsehood is easy to find, truth is hard to find
steps.stepSummary: Lies are everywhere, but truth is rare.
steps.simpleTranslation: Falsehood is common; truth is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The children answer: the letters of שקר are bunched together because lies are easy to find, and the letters of אמת are spread out because truth is hard to find.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Close letters stand for something you find right away. Letters scattered from the start of the alphabet to its end stand for something you must search the whole way to find.

phrases.english: Falsehood is common,
truth is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Letter spacing mirrors how common or rare each thing is: lies are close at hand, truth is far off.

steps.title: Why does falsehood stand on one leg while truth stands on bricks?
steps.stepSummary: The children ask why each letter of שקר rests on one point, while the letters of אמת have wide, solid bases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason that the letters of falsehood each stand on one leg, while the letters of truth stand on wide bases like bricks?
steps.whatsHappening: The children ask a second question, this time about the shape of the letters. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ש, ק, ר each touch the bottom line at only one narrow point. א, מ, ת rest on broad, flat bottoms, like bricks.

keyTerms.meaning: Built like bricks, on a wide base

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי טַעְמָא שִׁיקְרָא אַחֲדָא כַּרְעֵיהּ קָאֵי,
phrases.english: And what is the reason falsehood stands on one leg,
while truth is laid like bricks?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא שִׁיקְרָא אַחֲדָא כַּרְעֵיהּ קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question about the same two words, now about letter shape instead of letter order.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the different shapes of the letters of שקר and אמת.

steps.title: Truth lasts, falsehood does not
steps.stepSummary: Truth stands firm and lasts; a lie cannot stand for long.
steps.simpleTranslation: Truth stands; falsehood does not stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The children answer that אמת has a solid base because truth lasts, while שקר stands on one leg because a lie eventually falls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two answers teach complementary lessons. Lies are easy to find (step 30), but they do not last. Truth is hard to find, but once it is found it endures.
steps.whatToRemember: שקר: its letters are close together (lies are common) and stand on one leg (lies don't last). אמת: its letters are spread out (truth is rare) and stand on solid bases (truth endures).

phrases.english: Truth stands,
falsehood does not stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The letter shapes show that truth endures and falsehood collapses.

steps.title: The reversed-alphabet code describing the wicked
steps.stepSummary: Using the אתב"ש code, the letter pairs are read as God's response to a רשע: why should I love, rest My name on, pity, or spare one who rejected Me?
steps.simpleTranslation: Alef-Tav, Beit-Shin: He despised Me, so shall I desire him? Beit-Shin: He did not desire Me, so shall My name rest on him? Gimmel-Reish: He defiled his body, so shall I have mercy on him? Dalet-Kuf: He locked My doors, so shall I not cut off his horns? Up to here is the description of the wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new letter game called אתב"ש, which pairs the first letter with the last, the second with the second-to-last, and so on. Each pair is read as a word in a rhetorical question God asks about a רשע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair hints at words in the sentence: א and ת in אותי תעב and אתאוה; ב and ש in בי and שמי; ג and ר in גופו and ארחם; ד and ק in דלתותי and קרניו. The point is measure for measure: someone who pushes God away cannot expect God's closeness. The closing line, עד כאן מדת רשעים, tells us a second, opposite reading is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: A code pairing the first letter with the last, the second with the second-to-last, and so on
He locked My doors (shut out God's service)
His horns, meaning his power or pride
The way the wicked are dealt with

steps.confusionAlert: The letter pairs are not full words standing on their own. Each pair only hints at the first letters of words in the sentence the גמרא builds around it.

phrases.english: Alef-Tav, Beit-Shin (the reversed-alphabet code):
He despised Me, shall I desire him?
Beit-Shin: he did not desire Me,
shall My name rest upon him?
Gimmel-Reish: he defiled his body,
shall I have mercy on him?
Dalet-Kuf: he locked My doors,
shall I not cut off his horns?
Up to here is the attribute of the wicked.

steps.triggerLanguage: א״ת ב״ש: — אוֹתִי תִּעֵב אֶתְאַוֶּה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new way of reading the letters, the אתב"ש code, after the plain-order teachings end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Read through אתב"ש, the alphabet describes God turning away from a רשע measure for measure.

steps.title: The same code describing the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The same letter pairs are now read positively: one who feels shame before God will live in the heavens, be shielded from God's anger, and not be shaken by the שטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the attribute of the righteous: א״ת ב״ש: If you are ashamed (of sin). ג״ר ד״ק: If you do so, you will dwell in the heavens. ה״ץ ו״ף: There will be a barrier between you and (God's) anger. ז״ע ח״ס ט״ן: And you will not tremble before the שטן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the same אתב"ש pairs, and continues further down the alphabet, as a description of the reward of the צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same letters that described rejection now describe protection. Shame before God (בושה) is the first step, and it earns a place in heaven (דוק, as in 'He stretches out the heavens כדוק'), a shield from God's anger (אף), and safety from the שטן. The lesson: the same alphabet can spell punishment or reward, depending on how a person lives.

keyTerms.meaning: The way the righteous are dealt with
The accuser, the force of evil

phrases.english: But the attribute of the righteous:
Alef-Tav, Beit-Shin: if you are ashamed.

phrases.aramaic: ג״ר ד״ק — אִם אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן,
phrases.english: Gimmel-Reish, Dalet-Kuf: if you do so,
you will dwell in the heavens.
Heh-Tzadi, Vav-Peh:
there will be a barrier between you and (God's) anger.
Zayin-Ayin, Chet-Samech, Tet-Nun:
and you will not tremble before the Satan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, positive reading of the same letter pairs that step 33 read negatively.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Read through אתב"ש, the alphabet also promises shelter and reward to the צדיקים.

steps.title: גיהנם asks to swallow everyone
steps.stepSummary: The minister of גיהנם tells God: throw everyone, even the righteous, into the 'sea' of punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: י״ם כ״ל: The minister of גיהנם said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: רבונו של עולם, into the sea with all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The letters י-ם and כ-ל are read as ים כל, 'a sea for all.' The minister of גיהנם uses this to ask God to send everyone, even the צדיקים, into גיהנם. This sets up God's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the reward of the צדיקים is described, גיהנם objects and demands everyone. In function this works like a challenge: why should anyone be spared? God's reply comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The minister (angel) in charge of Gehinnom
Into the sea, all of them

phrases.english: Yod-Mem, Kaf-Lamed:
The minister of Gehinnom said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe, into the sea with all!

steps.triggerLanguage: י״ם כ״ל — אָמַר שַׂר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the protection of the צדיקים described in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גיהנם demands everyone, including the צדיקים.

steps.title: God protects the righteous from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: God answers that He has mercy on the צדיקים because they rejected immorality; they are pure, honest, and righteous, so גיהנם has no share in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: אח״ס בט״ע גי״ף: I have mercy on them because they kicked away immorality. דכ״ץ: They are pure, they are honest, they are righteous. הל״ק: You have no share in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The letters are now read in groups of three, and God uses them to reject גיהנם's demand and defend the צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new letter groups spell אני חס (I have mercy), בעטו (they kicked away), and גיף (immorality). Next come דכים, כנים, צדיקים (pure, honest, righteous). Last, ה-ל-ק hints at חלק (a share), since ה and ח sound alike. God tells גיהנם it has no portion in these people.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Alef-Chet-Samech, Beit-Tet-Ayin, Gimmel-Yod-Peh:
I have mercy on them
because they kicked away immorality.
Dalet-Kaf-Tzadi: they are pure,
they are honest, they are righteous.
Heh-Lamed-Kuf: you have no share in them.
phrases.notes: ה is read as ח to make חלק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: אח״ס בט״ע גי״ף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: God rejects גיהנם's demand from step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The צדיקים are spared because of their purity and their rejection of immorality; גיהנם has no claim on them.

steps.title: גיהנם asks to be fed from humanity
steps.stepSummary: גיהנם answers God: My Master, then feed me from the descendants of שת.
steps.simpleTranslation: ומרז״ן ש״ת: גיהנם said before Him: רבונו של עולם, my Master, feed me from the seed of שת.
steps.whatsHappening: The last letters of the alphabet are read as גיהנם's final plea: if it cannot have the צדיקים, let it be fed from the descendants of שת, meaning humanity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ו-מ-ר hints at אמר and מרי (my Master), ז-ן at זנני (feed me), and ש-ת at שת. The alphabet ends with this request. The dialogue shows God's protection of the צדיקים alongside גיהנם's continuing hunger for those who do not earn that protection.

keyTerms.meaning: The descendants of Seth, meaning all of humanity

steps.whatToRemember: The אתב"ש code first describes how the רשעים are rejected and then how the צדיקים are rewarded and shielded. Next, the אח"ס בט"ע grouping sets up a dialogue in which God refuses to hand the צדיקים over to גיהנם. Steps 38–40 continue that dialogue.

phrases.english: Vav-Mem-Reish-Zayin-Nun, Shin-Tav:
Gehinnom said before Him:
Master of the Universe, my Master,
feed me from the seed of Seth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: גיהנם responds to God's refusal in step 36 with a new request, which completes the alphabet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גיהנם asks to be fed from humanity, the descendants of שת, completing the אח"ס בט"ע reading.

steps.title: God refuses: the righteous go to the garden of myrtle
steps.stepSummary: God answers גיהנם's request with the pairs א״ל ב״ם (אל בם, 'not with them') and ג״ן ד״ס (גן הדס, 'the garden of myrtle'), meaning גן עדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: God said to him: א״ל ב״ם: 'Not with them.' ג״ן ד״ס: 'To where will I lead them? To the גן הדס (garden of myrtle).'
steps.whatsHappening: God answers גיהנם's last request to be fed from the descendants of שת by refusing. He says the righteous are not for גיהנם, and He will lead them to גן עדן instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא switches to a new letter code, אלב״ם, which pairs the first half of the alphabet with the second half. Read together, the letters spell אל בם, meaning 'you have no share in them,' and גן הדס, a poetic name for גן עדן. So the very letters of the alphabet become God's protective answer for the צדיקים.

keyTerms.meaning: A letter code that pairs א with ל, ב with מ, and so on (first half of the alphabet with the second half)
'Not with them' / 'not over them,' meaning you have no portion in them
Garden of myrtle, a poetic name for גן עדן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to read these pairs with the earlier codes (אתב״ש or אח״ס בט״ע) from the previous steps. Here the pairing is אלב״ם: א-ל, ב-מ, ג-נ, ד-ס, ה-ע, ו-פ, ז-צ, ח-ק, ט-ר, י-ש, כ-ת.

phrases.english: He said to him: Alef-lamed, beit-mem
phrases.notes: Read as אל בם: you have no share in them.

phrases.english: Gimmel-nun, dalet-samekh: to where will I lead them?
To the garden of myrtle.
phrases.notes: גן הדס means גן עדן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: א״ל ב״ם ג״ן ד״ס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: God answers גיהנם's request from step 37 to be fed from the descendants of שת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, the righteous are not yours; I will lead them to גן עדן.

steps.title: גיהנם complains that it is tired
steps.stepSummary: Through the pairs ה״ע ו״ף (עיף), the minister of גיהנם tells God: 'I am tired.'
steps.simpleTranslation: ה״ע ו״ף: גיהנם said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: רבונו של עולם, I am tired.
steps.whatsHappening: גיהנם pushes back after being refused and complains that it is weary and needs to be fed. This sets up God's final answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters ה-ע and ו-פ in the אלב״ם code produce the word עָיֵף, 'tired.' גיהנם is pressing its demand again, now as a complaint rather than a request. It is hinting that without people it remains hungry and weary.

keyTerms.meaning: Gehenna, the place of punishment (here, its minister speaking)

phrases.english: Heh-ayin, vav-peh:
phrases.notes: Spells עיף, 'tired.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר גֵּיהִנָּם לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Gehenna said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe, I am tired.

steps.triggerLanguage: ה״ע ו״ף אָמַר גֵּיהִנָּם לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: גיהנם responds to God's refusal with a renewed complaint.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גיהנם claims it is weary and still needs to be fed.

steps.title: God protects יצחק's descendants and offers the nations instead
steps.stepSummary: With ז״ץ ח״ק (זרעו של יצחק), God says these are the descendants of יצחק. With ט״ר י״ש כ״ת, He says: wait, I have many groups of the nations to give you.
steps.simpleTranslation: ז״ץ ח״ק: These are the descendants of יצחק. ט״ר י״ש כ״ת: Wait, I have groups upon groups of the אומות העולם that I will give you.
steps.whatsHappening: God gives His final answer. He will not give up the descendants of יצחק, but He tells גיהנם to wait, because He has plenty of groups from the nations to give it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters ז-צ and ח-ק hint to זרע and יצחק, which marks the people being protected. The letters ט-ר, י-ש, כ-ת spell טר ('wait'), יש ('there is'), and כיתות ('groups'). This closes the dialogue: the whole alphabet has been used to show God shielding the righteous and the descendants of יצחק from גיהנם.
steps.whatToRemember: Several letter codes (אתב״ש, then אח״ס בט״ע, then אלב״ם) are used to read the alphabet as lessons about the רשעים and the צדיקים, ending in a dialogue in which God defends the righteous and the descendants of יצחק from גיהנם.

phrases.english: of the nations of the world that I will give you.

steps.triggerLanguage: ז״ץ ח״ק הַלָּלוּ זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The descendants of יצחק are protected; גיהנם must wait and will receive groups from the nations instead.
